lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use carnivorous traps plus a 2-stamen spurred zygomorphic flower to make Lentibulariaceae unmistakable within Lamiales.

project_scope.note: The current project pool contains only Utricularia gibba; Kew accepts it and lists Texas within its native range.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Before the flower, look for carnivorous trap structures. In Utricularia, tiny bladder traps occur along finely divided aquatic shoots. Then confirm a bilabiate/spurred fused flower with only 2 stamens.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Carnivorous herbs, aquatic/terrestrial/epiphytic depending on genus. Utricularia is rootless and often has finely divided submerged shoots bearing bladder traps.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and zygomorphic; corolla fused, commonly 2-lipped and spurred or saccate; stamens 2; ovary superior, one-locular with free-central placentation.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a capsule with numerous seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Bladder trap + spurred bilabiate flower + two stamens is one of the cleanest Lamiales family combinations.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: carnivorous bladder → rootless aquatic shoot → yellow spurred flower → 2 stamens → capsule
visual_lesson.intro: Bladderwort is easiest when you learn the trap first. The flower then tells you it still belongs inside Lamiales.

steps.title: 1 · Find the bladder traps
steps.look_for: Tiny hollow bladders attached along thin branching submerged shoots.
steps.why_it_matters: The trap itself essentially announces Lentibulariaceae in the local aquatic flora.

steps.title: 2 · Notice the rootless body plan
steps.look_for: Fine threadlike stolons/shoots without ordinary true roots.
steps.why_it_matters: This prevents confusion with ordinary submerged aquatics.

steps.title: 3 · Read the yellow spurred flower
steps.look_for: A small yellow bilabiate fused corolla with a distinct spur.
steps.why_it_matters: The flower reconnects this bizarre carnivorous aquatic to the Lamiales blueprint.

steps.title: 4 · Count only two stamens
steps.look_for: Two fertile stamens inside the corolla tube.
steps.why_it_matters: This helps separate bladderwort from many 4-stamen bilabiate Lamiales.

comparisons.title: Lentibulariaceae vs Plantaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have bilabiate/spurred flowers, but Lentibulariaceae has carnivorous traps and only two stamens in the Utricularia pattern.

comparisons.title: Utricularia vs ordinary submerged aquatics
comparisons.rule: Utricularia is rootless and bears true bladder traps; Potamogeton, Vallisneria and other common aquatics do not.

visual_lesson.caveat: Not every Lentibulariaceae genus has bladder traps—Pinguicula uses sticky glandular leaves and Genlisea uses underground lobster-pot traps. The project genus Utricularia is the bladder-bearing branch.

genera.fast_cue: rootless aquatic shoot + bladder traps + yellow spurred 2-stamen flower

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label trap opening, trigger hairs if visible, and attachment to shoot
